description:
A ⁠United States submarine has sunk an Iranian warship with a torpedo in international waters off Sri Lanka’s coast, says US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
In a Pentagon briefing on Wednesday, Hegseth said the strike on the Iranian warship was the “first such attack on an enemy since World War II”.
Sri Lanka’s navy said 87 bodies had been recovered and 32 sailors were rescued after an Iranian military ship sank just outside the island’s territorial waters.
Authorities told Al Jazeera the frigate IRIS Dena, located about 40 nautical miles (75km) off Galle in southern Sri Lanka, sent out a distress call between 6am and 7am (00:30 to 01:30 GMT).
The ship had about 180 crew members on board, and a search and rescue operation was continuing, Sri Lankan officials said.

Al Jazeera’s Minelle Ferandez has more from Galle in Sri Lanka.

description:
Brian Mast, Republican chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee, told Al Jazeera that Iran has long posed an "imminent threat" to America, citing attacks on US vessels, the killing of three soldiers in Jordan, and failed negotiations. 
He defined the mission's objective as destroying "every single piece of Iranian military hardware" capable of reaching US forces or allies, including missiles, naval assets, and launchers. 
Mast expressed confidence in US intelligence and growing regional cooperation, arguing Gulf allies recognise America as their "hedge of protection" against Iran. He dismissed concerns about wider war, stating US capabilities are growing while Iran's diminish daily. 
On diplomacy, Mast said talks could resume only if Iran first agrees to abandon nuclear weapons, ballistic missiles, and support for proxies. He stressed the US would maintain military pressure throughout any negotiations.

description:
US President Donald Trump says he expects the operation in Iran to conclude within weeks, but America's history of foreign intervention suggests such campaigns rarely meet their stated goals. 
Past US invasions – from the Bay of Pigs to Vietnam, Iraq and Afghanistan – have shown that while initial military objectives may be achieved, long-term nation-building and stability often prove elusive. Historians warn that the US has repeatedly demonstrated the capacity to overthrow governments but lacks a reliable formula for creating successful successor states.

Al Jazeera's John Hendren reports from Washington, DC.

Senior Trump officials have held a second day of closed-door congressional briefings defending recent US strikes on Iran, but Democrats remain unconvinced and are pushing for a vote on a war powers resolution. Some Democratic senators expressed alarm that the operation could escalate into a ground war, while Republicans defended the timing and coordination with Israel. The administration has clarified conflicting explanations for the strikes, with officials citing both Israel's readiness to act independently and Iran's advancing weapons capabilities. Democrats accuse President Trump of breaching the constitution by authorising military action without congressional approval, and a vote is expected in the coming days that would order him to halt attacks on Iran.

Al Jazeera's Patty Culhane reports from Washington.

Hegseth declared that US and Israeli forces have achieved "uncontested airspace" over Iran, allowing round-the-clock strikes on missile systems, leadership, and military infrastructure. 
He claimed Iran's navy has been "decimated" and its air force destroyed, including the sinking of its flagship Soleimani by a US submarine torpedo—the first such sinking since WWII. 
General Caine reported over 2,000 targets hit, Iranian missile launches down 86%, and drone attacks down 73%.

Hegseth warned this is "only the beginning," with more strikes to come, and confirmed the killing of an Iranian operative linked to an assassination plot against President Trump. 
Both stressed the campaign would continue until Iran's missile and nuclear capabilities are eliminated.
